messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert triggered — increased 5xx rate from external cache provider impacting token bucket checkouts in rate-limiter-service. Alert details: provider: cachecorp-redis (managed), region: eu-west-1, 5xx spike > 8% for 3m. Incident ID: INC-2026-1771012345
jamie: acked. I'm oncall. seeing spikes in rate-limiter-service 5xx when calling cache backend. hitting errors on token fetch path -> fallback returns errors upstream.
jamie: quick triage: root cause appears to be upstream Redis managed instance saturating connections / timing out. provider status page shows partial degraded status: https://status.cachecorp.example/incidents/9876
jamie: impact summary: auth rate limiting calls failing -> clients see increased 429/503 depending on downstream handling. internal dashboards: ~12% of requests to /token/check failing, latency up from 30ms -> 600ms+.
priya: oncall takeover in 10. ping me if you need handoff. I can start mitigation and customer comms.
jamie: handing off to priya — current mitigations in progress:
- switched rate-limiter to read-through stale-mode for 10m (serve cached token verdicts) via feature flag
- increased local in-memory token cache size and TTL to reduce backend calls
- disabled noncritical telemetry that spikes on 5xx to reduce pressure

jamie: commands run:
```
# flip FF to degraded mode
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/flags/rate_limiter_degraded -d '{"enabled":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN'
# bump local cache
kubectl -n prod patch deploy rate-limiter --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"rate-limiter","env":[{"name":"LOCAL_TOKEN_CACHE_SIZE","value":"20000"},{"name":"LOCAL_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL_SEC","value":"600"}]}}]}}}'
```
ops-bot: @jamie toggled flag rate_limiter_degraded -> true
ops-bot: deploy patch applied to rate-limiter (rollout started)
priya: saw error rate drop a bit after degraded mode. still seeing intermittent 502/504 when our service talks to provider.
priya: next steps I will: open a replace path for token validation (use fallback in-memory only for unknown clients), and route non-critical traffic to dedicated token service in us-east to reduce cross-region retries.
priya: opened ticket with provider: https://support.cachecorp.example/tickets/34521 — assigned to CacheCorp SRE. reference: INC-2026-1771012345. provider acknowledges throttling at their edge.
evansre: tagging in to help with routing. Suggest enabling the short-circuit flow we discussed in runbook: if cache call returns >= 3 errors in 30s for a client, switch that client to local bucket and queue writes for async sync.
evansre: adding config patch (rolling):
```
{"rate_limiter": {"failure_threshold":3, "failure_window_sec":30, "fallback":"local_async_sync"}}
```
evansre: applying to canary (pod 5/6) now.
jamie: customer impact note: Enterprise customers using strict per-user limits (AcmeCorp and Brightside) saw elevated auth latency and a few short-lived rate limiter false positives. CS notified. no data loss. Metrics: AcmeCorp saw 7% additional auth failures in last 20m.
caroline-cs: I'm on comms with AcmeCorp, sending an interim status: "We are operating in degraded mode due to a third-party cache provider issue. We have switched to local fallback for rate limiting; you may see elevated latency. Mitigations are in place. We'll follow up with timeline and RCA." Will escalate if they threaten rollback.
priya: enabling dedicated failover route for token service for non-EU traffic to reduce load on eu-west provider. rolling traffic shift via LB: 15% -> 50% over next 10m.
priya: command to shift:
```
# adjust traffic weights
curl -X POST https://lb.internal/api/weights -d '{"service":"token-service","weights":{"eu-west":50,"us-east":50}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $LB_TOKEN'
```
ops-bot: Traffic weights updated: token-service -> eu-west 50%, us-east 50% (requested by priya)
jamie: quick note: enabled extended retry/backoff to avoid thundering herd while provider recovers: SDK retries from 3 -> 6, backoff base 200ms -> 500ms.
jamie: mapped impact to support SLAs: non-critical endpoints delayed, critical auths gently degraded. No active widespread data corruption or token misbehavior detected.
evansre: after canary update fallback behavior looks stable, error-rate trending down to 3-4%.
priya: provider status updated: "Partial throttling resolved, we are rolling fixes". cachecorp support estimates a full recovery in 45-60m. opened for priority track.
priya: I'll prepare post-incident notes and actions: vendor retry policies, per-tenant circuit breaker thresholds, and additional dedicated capacity for token-service to avoid cross-region reliance.
jamie: immediate action items recorded:
- (priya) Confirm provider SLA case and ETA, capture ticket updates.
- (evan) Add per-tenant circuit-breaker default (3 errors -> fallback) and monitor.
- (caroline-cs) Customer comms follow-ups for AcmeCorp / Brightside.
- (infra) Evaluate adding a lightweight local redis fallback for token-cache in eu-west to reduce third-party dependencies.
priya: handover to evan for next hour of watch. I'll remain on slack until provider resolved.
evansre: ack takeover. monitoring dashboards and the error budget page are on my watch: https://dashboards.internal/rate-limiter/errors
incident-bot: Note: handoff recorded — from priya to evansre at 1771014000
evansre: will keep the degraded flag on for 30m post-recovery to avoid flapping, and then gradually revert once provider confirms stable for 30m.
caroline-cs: AcmeCorp updated. They want an ETA; gave them current provider ETA (45-60m) and our mitigations. they're okay but asked for RCA timeline.
ops-bot: provider ticket 34521 updated by CacheCorp SRE: "Investigating connection pool exhaustion due to upstream EC2 instance warm-restart. Mitigations in progress." link: https://support.cachecorp.example/tickets/34521
evansre: observed stable behavior for 20m, errors down to 1.2% and latency back to ~40-70ms for most flows. leaving degraded mode on until provider confirms. will mark incident triage in 30m.
priya: provider status now: "Services returning to normal" — still watching.
jamie: thanks all. once provider fully recovered, we'll schedule a follow-up to update the runbook and add vendor-specific playbooks for connection pool exhaustion. Also need a short postmortem: assign owners.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1771012345 status -> acknowledged -> mitigated (partial) at 1771015400
priya: logging final notes: no customer data exposed. main impact: transient auth failures and elevated latency for a subset of EU customers. root cause: provider-side connection pool exhaustion during edge restart. proposed follow-ups: vendor retry tuning, local fallback TTL tuning, runbook addition.
evansre: closing watch. handing back to oncall rotation. last checks show metrics stable.
incident-bot: incident closed for paging at 1771015945 (monitoring continued).
